chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Miskān, from Yaʿqūb al-Bazzāz, who said:

I said to him: I rise shortly before dawn and pray four rakʿahs, then I fear that dawn may break. Should I begin with the witr, or complete the rakʿahs? He said: No, rather perform the witr and delay the rakʿahs until you make them up in the early part of the day.

So the proper way regarding this narration is that we interpret it as referring to what is more virtuous, because what is more virtuous is that one perform the obligatory prayer at the beginning of its time, and the first narration is a concession, as we explained before this.

key_terms.الرَّكَعَاتِ: the prayer units being completed or postponed
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn; the onset of the fajr time
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةَ: the obligatory prayer, here referring to the fajr prayer
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: that which is more virtuous or preferable in practice
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the witr prayer performed as the concluding unit of the night prayer
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: a concession or allowance in legal practice
key_terms.صَدْرِ النَّهَارِ: the early part of the daytime, when the missed rakʿahs may be made up

ai.seo_question: If fajr is about to break during salat al-layl, should one pray witr first or complete the remaining rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for one praying salat al-layl when the time of fajr approaches before completion. It instructs giving priority to the witr and postponing the remaining rakʿahs to the daytime, while explaining that this reflects the more virtuous practice of performing the obligatory prayer at its earliest time.
